items.excerpt: OpenAI's first hardware product is reportedly a portable, screenless 'AI companion' speaker: per Bloomberg it runs an advanced GPT-Live voice mode, has moving mechanical parts to feel 'alive,' and packs cameras and sensors for contextual awareness.
OpenAI's debut device is framed less as a smart speaker and more as a proactive AI companion — a mobile, context-aware gadget (co-designed with Jony Ive's io) expected to launch in 2027.

A leak describes OpenAI's first hardware as a movable, screenless smart speaker built as a physical ChatGPT companion that can control smart-home appliances, play media and answer questions — half-speaker, half-robot.

Analysis argues OpenAI's camera-and-sensor smart speaker would partly overlap with Apple's upcoming AirPods Ultra — but that a wearable form factor is more practical for portable AI than a device you have to carry around.

OpenAI's first shipping hardware is the Codex Micro, a $230 keypad built with Work Louder to drive its agentic coding tool — customizable LED-status keys, a dial for reasoning levels and a joystick for navigating agent workflows.

Google's Gemma 4 E2B runs directly on the Pixel 10's Tensor G5 TPU, enabling on-device offline AI chat, image recognition and voice transcription with no internet connection — a push for local, private generative AI on the phone.

After a year's delay, Apple's rebuilt Siri AI — now powered by Google's Gemini models — ships in iOS 27; a month of use finds it genuinely useful for searching personal data and multi-step tasks, though still short of flawless.

Meta starts charging $20/month for Meta One Premium, gating the smart glasses' AI 'Conversation Focus' feature to just 3 hours/month free (15 hours paid) — a look at how on-device AI capabilities on wearables are being monetized.
